data.StoryText: Franklin and other colonial leaders reconvene the Albany Congress.
The Ohio Company of Virginia seeks a western land grant.
Boston merchants demand redress for the Tea Party.
Militia reports a skirmish on the western frontier.
The Virginia House of Burgesses is called into session.
Philadelphia merchants convene at the coffee house.
Yamassee raiders strike the Florida frontier.
St. Augustine's coquina walls crumble in a storm.
A Spanish convoy is lost at sea near Pensacola.
A Creek embassy arrives at Pensacola.
Apalachee mission converts return to Florida.
Florida cattle drives boom on the open range.
Marquis de Montcalm lands at Quebec with regulars.
Beaver pelt prices fall in Montreal.
A fire breaks out at Trois-Rivières.
A new militia levy is called at Quebec.
A great council convenes at Pays d'en Haut.
A silver strike is announced at San Luis Potosí.
A royal visita arrives in Mexico City.
Apache raiders strike the Texas frontier.
The Manila galleon arrives at Acapulco.
The expulsion of Jesuits echoes through the missions.
A grain riot breaks out at Querétaro.
The Onondaga council fire is rekindled by the sachems.
A Beaver War skirmish erupts on the frontier.
The Two Row wampum belt is renewed at Onondaga.
A sachem succession crisis unfolds in the Seneca nation.
The annual Sun Dance is held on the open prairie.
A Lakota band migrates to new hunting grounds.
A great plains bison hunt is organized.
Creek refugees from the south seek shelter with the Cherokee.
The Cherokee Phoenix press prints its first broadside.
Dragging Canoe's warband strikes the Cumberland settlements.
The first salmon of the year run at Celilo Falls.
A canoe embassy arrives from the coast.
A new cedar longhouse is built at the council grounds.
The wapato fields yield a bountiful harvest.
Trade canoes reach the falls with goods from the coast.
A whale hunter returns with news of the sea.
A silver strike is announced at Potosí.
Lima's reconstruction is debated in the cabildo.
Cinchona bark is shipped from Callao to Spain.
The Cusco cathedral is consecrated by the bishop.
The Arequipa wool fair convenes in the plaza.
Túpac Amaru II's execution echoes through the audiencia.
Gold is struck at Minas Gerais.
Quilombo dos Palmares is disbanded by the captain-major.
The Salvador sugar fleet sails for Lisbon.
Cocoa is planted in the Manaus backlands.
The Sete Povos Jesuit reductions are reorganized.
Conde de Lippe drills the colonial militia at Rio.
The Parliament of Loncos convenes on the open ground.
The Parliament of Quilin reopens the frontier.
A Mapuche cavalry raid sweeps the Spanish frontier.
The Bio-Bio wheat harvest is blessed.
A toqui council convenes at Concepción.
Mestizo settlements expand along the Bio-Bio.
An echo of the Cartagena siege reaches the audiencia.
The Comunero revolt echoes in Tunja and Socorro.
The Bogotá cathedral is consecrated by the archbishop.
The Muzo emerald mine reopens under royal license.
Cacao plantations flourish along the Magdalena.
The Quito Audiencia convenes a special session.
A great band crosses the Chaco toward the Pilcomayo.
The Wichí trade fair convenes at the river.
The honey and wax harvest completes.
A frontier treaty is negotiated with Salta.
The yerba mate groves yield a fine harvest.
Guayacán wood is cut along the Paraná.
